data.reasoning: Report 2 (deepseek) successfully reviewed all 3 files and found no security issues. Reports 1 and 3 had API errors preventing full review, but their initial PKGBUILD audits (which did succeed) both found it safe. The package is a standard Rust AUR package with pinned checksums, source URLs pointing to the project's own GitHub repository, and no dangerous patterns (no curl/wget/eval/base64, no command substitution at global scope). The .nvchecker.toml is a normal version-checking config. No injection patterns detected.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by API infrastructure failures, not security concerns. Reports 1 and 3 experienced HTTP 400/429 errors that prevented full file review, resulting in inconclusive verdicts. Report 2 completed successfully and found the package safe. All three reports' initial PKGBUILD audits succeeded and agreed it was safe.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen): API errors (HTTP 400) prevented review of PKGBUILD and .nvchecker.toml
Report 3 (openrouter): API errors (parse failure, HTTP 429) prevented review of PKGBUILD and .nvchecker.toml
learnings: API reliability directly impacts audit completeness - infrastructure failures should not override successful initial audits when they agree
When one model completes full review successfully and initial audits from other models agree, that provides sufficient confidence for a verdict
Standard Rust PKGBUILDs with pinned checksums and GitHub sources are low-risk patterns that models should recognize confidently
